meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so we have twenty-five minutes. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who decided on that mark, and when?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. Was Owen heard before that mark went in, and on what basis was it entered?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.

"Like, being stuck" is not a wrong answer, Hale, and a seventeen-year-old cornered by his teacher with no warning blanks on a paragraph number. I want to see the note you wrote that day, with the date on it. What else did you base the zero on besides that and the software?
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
Students change their thesis between an outline and a final draft, Hale; that's what outlines are for. I'm writing down October 15. Put the outline and the essay side by side in front of me.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

That's 4.4, and I want it in writing before Thursday morning, not after, saying nothing is on his record now or later. Thursday at 8:15 in your room means no other students present, Hale, and I want that in the email too. I'm not agreeing to anything until you show me the outline and the essay side by side.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you offered Owen a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record, and you committed to putting that in writing by Friday at 3 PM. I still require that written confirmation before the rewrite, stating that no other students will be present and that nothing is on Owen's record now or will be later, and I still expect to see his October 15 outline and his essay side by side. I expect that in writing before Thursday morning.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback position. Your commitment to procedure 4.4 met her demand that this stay off his record and stay quiet, but she had not accepted the rewrite. She still wants the promise in writing before Thursday morning, with no other students present, and she still wants to see the outline and the essay side by side. That is close to the fair outcome of a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record, but it was not settled.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling home in one sentence and then gave her dated, specific evidence tied to Owen's own work, which turned her from attacking the zero to setting terms.
What cost ground: You made the offer before putting either document in front of her, so she had nothing she could read and check herself and kept her acceptance back.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your evidence, the October 15 outline and the November 2 conversation, never came near a late night in October. That night proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When you raised the October 15 outline, show her the outline and the essay side by side on screen before you make the rewrite offer.
